column1: # What a long Treasury DID across the equity drawdowns of the last 24 years, on the model bond's
# footing: for every equity peak-to-trough decline of 15% or worse, the bond's LOG return over the
# same span, in percent, the fund's empirical duration over that span and the inflation the decline
# was seen under. The model's bond is a 13.5-year bond (`DURATION_REF`), so each episode is read as
# bondPct x 13.5 / duration -- an unscaled TLT number reads a 13.5-year bond against a 17-year
# fund's move -- and the crash fit (`crash_fit`: Theil-Sen of the scaled moves on cpiTrough, by the
# model's own median) reads +7.10 at 2% inflation and -6.07 per point. REPORTED beside the graded
# `bond crash at 2% infl` and `bond crash per % infl` rows, never graded: six episodes, one of them
# seen above 4%, are too few to grade. The graded records are the same reading since 1962
# (crash-response-1962-2026-10-05.tsv, crash-response-1962-hitec-2026-10-06.tsv).
# `BondCrashSuite` / `bond_crash_tests` re-derive the fit from the rows below.
# Equity SPY, bond TLT, daily Yahoo adjusted closes over their overlap, 2002-07-30..2026-08-03.
# duration: TLT's empirical duration over the episode, in years -- minus the slope of its weekly
#   (5-session) log return on the weekly change of the 20-year constant-maturity Treasury yield
#   (FRED DGS20), over peak..trough. This is the sensitivity that turned the yield path into
#   bondPct, so it is the like-for-like scale; the fund's published effective duration moved
#   between 15 and 19 over these years (14.89 on 2026-08-22, ishares-2026-08-22.tsv).
# cpiPeak / cpiTrough: CPI year over year at the peak and the trough, percent (FRED CPIAUCSL, the
#   last monthly observation dated on or before the day against the one twelve months earlier).
# regime: inflation when CPI year over year rose over the decline and stood at 4% or more at the
#   trough, else growth -- informational: the fit reads cpiTrough, not the regime.
peak
